### Network 5: Hernandez et al. 2025

We read a microbial association network from a research paper where the data is provided as an edge list. Each row represents an association between two microbial taxa, along with the strength of that association.

Link to data: https://github.com/clayton-lab/marm_microbiome_metabolome_manuscript/blob/main/results/node_properties/associations.tsv

The edge list is converted directly into an undirected graph. We then obtain basic network properties such as the number of nodes and edges.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read the edge list
edges <- read.delim("data/05-hernandez/associations.tsv")

# Look at the first few associations
head(edges)

# Keep only associations between microbial genera
# This removes metabolite-metabolite and metabolite-genera associations
edges_genera <- edges[edges$interaction_type == "genera-genera", ]

# Look at the filtered data
head(edges_genera)

# Create a microbiome-only network
# X_features and Y_features are the connected microbial genera
# association represents the strength of the relationship
g_hernandez <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges_genera[, c("X_features", "Y_features", "association")],
  directed = FALSE
)

# Count nodes
vcount(g_hernandez)

# Count edges
ecount(g_hernandez)

# Plot network
plot(g_hernandez, vertex.label = NA,  vertex.size = 5,)

# Degree
d5 <- mean(degree(g_hernandez))

# Closeness
c5 <- mean(closeness(g_hernandez, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 6: Lacruz-Pleguezuelos et al. 2026

We read a microbial association network from the MHOmicrobiome GitHub repository, where the data is provided as an edge list. Each row represents an association between two microbial taxa, along with the strength of that association.

Link to data: https://github.com/blacruz17/MHOmicrobiome/blob/main/data/edgeweights_mhno.csv

The edge list is converted directly into an undirected graph. We then obtain basic network properties such as the number of nodes and edges.

```{r}

# Look at the first few associations
head(edges_lacruz_pleguezuelos1)

# Create the network from the edge list
# v1 and v2 are the connected taxa
# edgeweight is stored as an edge weight
g_lacruz_pleguezuelos1 <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges_lacruz_pleguezuelos1[, c("v1", "v2", "edgeweight")], directed = FALSE)

# Count nodes
vcount(g_lacruz_pleguezuelos1)

# Count edges
ecount(g_lacruz_pleguezuelos1)

# Plot network

# Degree
d6 <- mean(degree(g_lacruz_pleguezuelos1))

# Closeness
c6 <- mean(closeness(g_lacruz_pleguezuelos1, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 11: Jeong et al. 2023

The original data was downloaded as a journal table CSV file. Because the journal table used merged-cells, the raw CSV files were cleaned into standard edge lists before being read into R. The cleaned edge list is then converted into an undirected graph. We then obtain the number of nodes and edges.

Link to data: https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/figure/10.1080/20002297.2023.2186591?scroll=top&needAccess=true

This table represents the compositional network between bacterial genera within the S type oral microbiome.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read the cleaned edge list
edges_jeong_s_type <- read.csv("data/11-jeong/jeong_s_type_edges.csv")

# Look at the first few associations
head(edges_jeong_s_type)

# Create the network from the edge list
# Source and target are the connected bacterial genera
# Weight is the SparCC R-value
# Sign indicates whether the association is positive or negative
g_jeong_s_type <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges_jeong_s_type[, c("source", "target", "weight", "sign")], directed = FALSE)

# Count nodes
vcount(g_jeong_s_type)

# Count edges
ecount(g_jeong_s_type)

# Plot network
# Ignore edge weights when determining the layout because some weights are negative
plot(
  g_jeong_s_type,
  layout = layout_with_fr(g_jeong_s_type, weights = NA)
)

# Degree
d11 <- mean(degree(g_jeong_s_type))

# Closeness
c11 <- mean(closeness(g_jeong_s_type, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 18: Ruiz-Perez et al. 2021

We read a network from a research paper where the data is given in GraphML format. The network contains microbial taxa, genes, metabolites, and host features as nodes. Edges represent inferred relationships from a Dynamic Bayesian Network.

Link to data: https://github.com/DaniRuizPerez/PALM-Public-Respository/blob/master/Networks/HEGTM/3Parents/human_ibd_microbiota_genes_metabolites_dbn_sample_alignment_sr14d_top100x100_host_taxa_reference_dbnIntraBoot.graphml

For this first analysis, we keep only the microbial taxa nodes so that this network is more comparable to the other microbiome networks in the project.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read GraphML network
net_ruiz_perez <- read_graph("data/18-ruiz-perez/human_ibd_microbiota_genes_metabolites_dbn_sample_alignment_sr14d_top100x100_host_taxa_reference_dbnIntraBoot.graphml",
                             format = "graphml")

# Keep only microbial taxa nodes
taxa_nodes <- V(net_ruiz_perez)[grepl("^s__", V(net_ruiz_perez)$id)]

# Create microbiome-only network
net_ruiz_perez_taxa <- induced_subgraph(net_ruiz_perez, vids = taxa_nodes)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_ruiz_perez_taxa)

# Count edges
ecount(net_ruiz_perez_taxa)

# Plot network
plot(net_ruiz_perez_taxa, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d18 <- mean(degree(net_ruiz_perez_taxa))

# Closeness
c18 <- mean(closeness(net_ruiz_perez_taxa, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 19: Lymberopoulos et al. 2022

We read a gut microbiome co-enrichment network from a research paper. The network was created from gut microbiome samples using Topological Data Analysis, where connections represent co-enrichment relationships between microbial taxa.

Link to data: https://github.com/thesharmalab-team/microbiome_covid/blob/main/CovidTDA/data_and_scripts/binarised_coenrichment_GMrepo_TDA_PD.csv

The CSV file is read as an adjacency matrix and converted into an undirected igraph network. We then obtain basic network properties such as the number of nodes and edges.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read adjacency matrix
gut_data <- read.csv("data/19-lymberopoulos/binarised_coenrichment_GMrepo_TDA_PD.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# Keep only gut microbiome taxa
gut_data <- as.matrix(gut_data[1:985, 1:985])

# Create undirected network
net_lymberopoulos <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(gut_data, mode = "undirected", diag = FALSE)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_lymberopoulos)

# Count edges
ecount(net_lymberopoulos)

# Plot network
plot(net_lymberopoulos, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d19 <- mean(degree(net_lymberopoulos))

# Closeness
c19 <- mean(closeness(net_lymberopoulos, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 20: Loftus et al. 2021

We read a colorectal cancer gut microbiome bacterial association network from a research paper. The data contains pairs of associated bacterial species and their association weights.

Link to data: https://github.com/Markloftus/CancerMicrobiome/blob/main/Files/Dataframes/OnlyCRC_associations.csv

The bacterial pairs are separated into two columns to create an edge list. The edge list is then converted into an undirected `igraph` network.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read data
crc_data <- read.csv("data/20-loftus/OnlyCRC_associations.csv")

# Create edge list
crc_edges <- data.frame(bacteria1 = sub("<-->.*", "", crc_data[[1]]),
                        bacteria2 = sub(".*<-->", "", crc_data[[1]]),
                        weight = crc_data[[2]])

# Create network
net_loftus_crc <- graph_from_data_frame(crc_edges, directed = FALSE)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_loftus_crc)

# Count edges
ecount(net_loftus_crc)

# Plot network
plot(net_loftus_crc, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d20 <- mean(degree(net_loftus_crc))

# Closeness
c20 <- mean(closeness(net_loftus_crc, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Network 22: Ravikrishnan et al. 2021

We read a gut microbiome metabolic association network under DMEM conditions. The data contains pairs of gut microbial species and their Metabolic Support Index (MSI) values.

Link to data: https://github.com/aarthi31/gutmicrobiome/blob/master/MSIResults/edges_msi_benefit_dmem_withedgeval.txt

The microbial pairs are used as an edge list, with the MSI value as the edge weight. The edge list is then converted into a directed `igraph` network.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read DMEM interaction data
dmem_data <- read.table("data/22-ravikrishnan/edges_msi_benefit_dmem_withedgeval.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

# Create directed edge list
dmem_edges <- data.frame(from = dmem_data[[2]], to = dmem_data[[1]],weight = dmem_data[[3]])

# Create directed network
net_ravikrishnan_dmem <- graph_from_data_frame(dmem_edges, directed = TRUE)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_ravikrishnan_dmem)

# Count edges
ecount(net_ravikrishnan_dmem)

# Plot network
plot(net_ravikrishnan_dmem, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d22 <- mean(degree(net_ravikrishnan_dmem))

# Closeness
c22 <- mean(closeness(net_ravikrishnan_dmem, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Network 27: Li et al. 2019

We read a healthy human gut microbiome interaction network from a research paper. The network contains microbial species as nodes and directed Transfer Entropy relationships between species as edges.

Link to data: https://github.com/HokudaiNexusLab/Microbiome/tree/master/resultsNetwork

The node and edge CSV files are read into R and combined to create the network. The edge weights represent Transfer Entropy, which measures information flow between microbial species. The files are then converted into a directed `igraph` network.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Read nodes
healthy_nodes <- read.csv("data/27-li/Nodes_Healthy_Group_withoutC_C1.csv")

# Read edges
healthy_edges <- read.csv("data/27-li/Edges_Healthy_Group_withoutC_C1.csv")

# Create network
net_healthy <- graph_from_data_frame(healthy_edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = healthy_nodes)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_healthy)

# Count edges
ecount(net_healthy)

# Plot network
plot(net_healthy, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d27 <- mean(degree(net_healthy))

# Closeness
c27 <- mean(closeness(net_healthy, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Network 28: Li et al. 2019

We read an unhealthy IBS human gut microbiome interaction network from a research paper. The network contains microbial species as nodes and directed Transfer Entropy relationships between species as edges. The paper compares interaction networks across healthy and unhealthy microbiome states.

Link to data: https://github.com/HokudaiNexusLab/Microbiome/tree/master/resultsNetwork

The node and edge CSV files are read into R and combined to create the network. The edge weights represent Transfer Entropy, which measures information flow between microbial species. The files are then converted into a directed igraph network.

```{r}
# Read nodes
unhealthy_nodes <- read.csv("data/28-li/Nodes_MaxEnt_UnHealthy.csv")

# Read edges
unhealthy_edges <- read.csv("data/28-li/Edges_MaxEnt_UnHealthy.csv")

# Create network
net_unhealthy <- graph_from_data_frame(unhealthy_edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = unhealthy_nodes)

# Count nodes
vcount(net_unhealthy)

# Count edges
ecount(net_unhealthy)

# Plot network
plot(net_unhealthy, vertex.label = NA, vertex.size = 5)

# Degree
d28 <- mean(degree(net_unhealthy))

# Closeness
c28 <- mean(closeness(net_unhealthy, weights = NA), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Organizing networks into table

Here we organizing all igraph networks from smallest to largest (node count) and displaying them on a table.

```{r}
library(igraph)

all_objects <- mget(ls())

# Keep only objects that are igraph networks
networks <- Filter(
  function(x) inherits(x, "igraph"),
  all_objects
)

# Count how many networks were found
length(networks)

# Display the names of the networks
names(networks)

# Create table with network information
network_table <- data.frame(
  network = names(networks),
  nodes = sapply(networks, vcount),
  edges = sapply(networks, ecount)
)

# Sort networks from smallest to largest
network_table <- network_table[order(network_table$nodes), ]

# Display the table
network_table

nrow(network_table)
```

## Shared microbes across all networks (v3: species-level matching)

The genus-level networks (Hernandez, Jeong S-type and H-type) and Goyal are left out, and the remaining networks are matched at species level. A species counts as shared only if it appears in every remaining network. Set `match_level <- "genus"` to go back to genus matching.

Run this chunk after all network chunks and before the "Organizing networks into table" chunk. It replaces the earlier versions.

```{r}
library(igraph)

# ---- 1. Settings ------------------------------------------------------------

# "species" matches on "genus species"; "genus" matches on genus only
match_level <- "species"

# igraph objects that should NOT take part in the comparison:
# - net_goyal: numeric IDs and metabolites
# - g_hernandez, g_jeong_s_type, g_jeong_h_type: genus-level only
# - net_healthy, net_unhealthy (Li): nodes are bacterial families
# - net_lugo_martinez: nodes are bacterial classes plus clinical variables
# - net_ruiz_perez: full network with genes/metabolites; the taxa-only
#   version net_ruiz_perez_taxa is used instead
# - g_steinway: only 9 nodes
# - g, g_er: leftover helper / model objects, not real networks
exclude <- c("net_goyal", "g_hernandez", "g_jeong_s_type", "g_jeong_h_type",
             "net_healthy", "net_unhealthy", "net_lugo_martinez",
             "net_ruiz_perez", "g_steinway", "g", "g_er")

# Renamed / synonymous genera, written in lowercase as old = "new".
# Add entries as you discover mismatches in the near-miss table below.
genus_aliases <- c(
  "propionibacterium" = "cutibacterium"
)

# Labels that carry no taxonomic information
no_info <- c("uncultured", "unclassified", "unknown", "na")

# ---- 2. Collect the networks ------------------------------------------------

net_list <- Filter(function(x) inherits(x, "igraph"), mget(ls()))
net_list <- net_list[!(names(net_list) %in% exclude)]

length(net_list)
names(net_list)

# ---- 3. Helper functions ----------------------------------------------------

# Get node labels. Edge-list networks store them in "name"; GraphML networks
# store them in "id" or "label".
get_node_names <- function(g) {
  attrs <- vertex_attr_names(g)
  for (a in c("name", "id", "label")) {
    if (a %in% attrs) return(as.character(vertex_attr(g, a)))
  }
  stop("No name/id/label vertex attribute found")
}

# Turn each label into a character vector of lowercase taxa (possibly empty):
#   species level: "bacteroides fragilis"
#   genus level:   "bacteroides"
# Labels without enough information (e.g. "Bacteroides sp.") give an empty vector.
clean_taxa <- function(x, level = match_level) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))

  # Taxonomy strings: keep the part after s__ (species) or g__ (genus)
  tag <- if (level == "species") "s__" else "g__"
  has_tag <- grepl(tag, x, fixed = TRUE)
  x[has_tag] <- sub(paste0("^.*", tag, "([^;|,]*).*$"), "\\1", x[has_tag])

  # Leftover rank prefixes such as s__
  x <- sub("^[a-z]__", "", x)

  # Brackets and quotes, e.g. "[Eubacterium] rectale"
  x <- gsub("[][\"'()]", "", x)

  # Underscores and dots become spaces: "Bacteroides_fragilis" -> "Bacteroides fragilis"
  x <- gsub("[_.]+", " ", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(x))

  # "Candidatus Genus species" -> "Genus species"
  x <- sub("^Candidatus ", "", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- tolower(x)

  lapply(strsplit(x, " ", fixed = TRUE), function(w) {
    if (length(w) == 0 || is.na(w[1]) || !nzchar(w[1])) return(character(0))

    if (level == "genus") {
      # "escherichia-shigella" counts as both genera
      parts <- strsplit(w[1], "[-/]")[[1]]
      parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
      hit <- parts %in% names(genus_aliases)
      parts[hit] <- unname(genus_aliases[parts[hit]])
      return(unique(setdiff(parts, no_info)))
    }

    # Species level: needs a genus and a real species word
    if (w[1] %in% no_info || length(w) < 2) return(character(0))
    genus <- w[1]
    species <- w[2]
    if (species %in% c(no_info, "sp", "spp", "bacterium", "genomosp", "cf") ||
        grepl("^[0-9]", species)) return(character(0))
    if (genus %in% names(genus_aliases)) genus <- unname(genus_aliases[genus])
    paste(genus, species)
  })
}

# ---- 4. Add taxon labels to every node --------------------------------------

# taxa_all holds all matched taxa of a node, separated by ";"
net_list <- lapply(net_list, function(g) {
  V(g)$taxa_all <- vapply(clean_taxa(get_node_names(g)),
                          paste, character(1), collapse = ";")
  g
})

node_taxa <- function(g) strsplit(V(g)$taxa_all, ";", fixed = TRUE)

# Sanity check: original vs cleaned names for each network.
# A network with most nodes "unresolved" is probably not labeled at this level.
invisible(lapply(names(net_list), function(nm) {
  g <- net_list[[nm]]
  cat("\n", nm, "-", vcount(g), "nodes,", sum(V(g)$taxa_all == ""),
      "unresolved at", match_level, "level\n")
  print(head(data.frame(original = get_node_names(g), matched = V(g)$taxa_all), 4))
}))

# ---- 5. Find taxa shared by ALL networks ------------------------------------

taxon_sets <- lapply(net_list, function(g) unique(unlist(node_taxa(g))))

shared_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxon_sets)
length(shared_taxa)
shared_taxa

# How many networks each taxon appears in
taxon_presence <- sort(table(unlist(taxon_sets)), decreasing = TRUE)
head(taxon_presence, 20)

# Leave-one-out: size of the shared set if each network were left out.
# A big jump points at the network that limits the overlap.
leave_one_out <- sapply(names(taxon_sets), function(nm) {
  length(Reduce(intersect, taxon_sets[names(taxon_sets) != nm]))
})
sort(leave_one_out, decreasing = TRUE)

# Near misses: taxa present in every network except one.
# Look here for spelling variants or renamed genera, then add them to genus_aliases.
near_miss <- names(taxon_presence)[taxon_presence == length(net_list) - 1]
if (length(near_miss) > 0) {
  data.frame(
    taxon = near_miss,
    missing_from = vapply(near_miss, function(tx) {
      names(taxon_sets)[!vapply(taxon_sets, function(s) tx %in% s, logical(1))]
    }, character(1)),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

# ---- 6. Build filtered versions of each network -----------------------------

# Keep nodes with at least one shared taxon. Original nodes are kept as they
# are, so edges between them are preserved.
net_list_shared <- lapply(net_list, function(g) {
  keep <- vapply(node_taxa(g), function(tok) any(tok %in% shared_taxa), logical(1))
  induced_subgraph(g, V(g)[keep])
})

# Compare size before and after
shared_summary <- data.frame(
  network = names(net_list),
  nodes_before = sapply(net_list, vcount),
  edges_before = sapply(net_list, ecount),
  nodes_after = sapply(net_list_shared, vcount),
  edges_after = sapply(net_list_shared, ecount)
)
shared_summary

shared_taxa
```

## Export node and edge tables of all networks to CSV

Writes one combined CSV for nodes and one for edges, with a `network` column saying which network each row belongs to. Every vertex/edge attribute is included (columns that exist in only some networks are filled with NA). The node table also has the cleaned taxon labels, each node's degree, and whether the node is in the shared set.

Run this after the shared-nodes chunk (v3), because it uses `net_list`, `node_taxa()`, `get_node_names()` and `shared_taxa` from that chunk.

```{r}
library(igraph)

dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)

# This chunk needs the results of the shared-nodes v3 chunk. Stop early with a
# clear message if that chunk has not been run in this session.
if (!exists("net_list") || !exists("shared_taxa") ||
    !all(vapply(net_list, function(g) "taxa_all" %in% vertex_attr_names(g), logical(1)))) {
  stop("Run the shared-nodes v3 chunk first (it creates net_list, shared_taxa and taxa_all).")
}

# Helpers, repeated from the v3 chunk so this chunk also works if they are missing
get_node_names <- function(g) {
  attrs <- vertex_attr_names(g)
  for (a in c("name", "id", "label")) {
    if (a %in% attrs) return(as.character(vertex_attr(g, a)))
  }
  stop("No name/id/label vertex attribute found")
}

node_taxa <- function(g) strsplit(V(g)$taxa_all, ";", fixed = TRUE)

# Stack data frames that have different columns, filling gaps with NA
bind_fill <- function(dfs) {
  all_cols <- unique(unlist(lapply(dfs, names)))
  dfs <- lapply(dfs, function(d) {
    missing <- setdiff(all_cols, names(d))
    d[missing] <- NA
    d[all_cols]
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, dfs)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

# write.csv cannot handle list columns, so flatten them first
flatten_lists <- function(d) {
  d[] <- lapply(d, function(col) {
    if (is.list(col)) vapply(col, paste, character(1), collapse = ";") else col
  })
  d
}

# ---- Node table: one row per node, all vertex attributes --------------------

node_tables <- lapply(names(net_list), function(nm) {
  g <- net_list[[nm]]
  d <- as_data_frame(g, what = "vertices")
  d$node_label <- get_node_names(g)
  d$degree <- as.numeric(degree(g))
  d$in_shared_set <- vapply(node_taxa(g), function(tok) any(tok %in% shared_taxa), logical(1))
  d$network <- nm
  d <- flatten_lists(d)
  # Put the identifying columns first
  first_cols <- c("network", "node_label", "taxa_all", "in_shared_set", "degree")
  d[c(intersect(first_cols, names(d)), setdiff(names(d), first_cols))]
})

all_nodes <- bind_fill(node_tables)
write.csv(all_nodes, "output/all_network_nodes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

dim(all_nodes)
head(all_nodes)

# ---- Edge table: one row per edge, all edge attributes ----------------------

edge_tables <- lapply(names(net_list), function(nm) {
  d <- as_data_frame(net_list[[nm]], what = "edges")
  d$network <- nm
  d <- flatten_lists(d)
  d[c("network", setdiff(names(d), "network"))]
})

all_edges <- bind_fill(edge_tables)
write.csv(all_edges, "output/all_network_edges.csv", row.names = FALSE)

dim(all_edges)
head(all_edges)

# ---- Optional: one-row-per-network summary ----------------------------------

network_summary <- data.frame(
  network = names(net_list),
  nodes = sapply(net_list, vcount),
  edges = sapply(net_list, ecount),
  directed = sapply(net_list, is_directed),
  node_attributes = sapply(net_list, function(g) paste(vertex_attr_names(g), collapse = ";")),
  edge_attributes = sapply(net_list, function(g) paste(edge_attr_names(g), collapse = ";"))
)
write.csv(network_summary, "output/network_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
network_summary
```

```{r}
closeness_values <- c(c1, c5, c6, c7, c8, c9, c10, c11, c12, c13, c15, c18, c19, c20, c21, c22, c23, c27, c28)

hist(degree_values)
hist(closeness_values)
```

## Compute Degree Distribution

Degree measures how many connections each taxon has. This is one of the main features we will compare between microbiome networks and the simulated network models.

```{r}
# Compute degree
deg <- degree(g)
deg

summary(deg)

# Plot degree distribution
hist(deg, main = "Degree distribution", xlab = "Degree")
```

## Compute Clustering Coefficient

The clustering coefficient measures how connected neighboring taxa are to each other. This helps identify whether the microbiome network contains groups or clusters of highly connected taxa.

```{r}
# Compute clustering coefficient
clustering <- transitivity(g, type = "local", isolates = "zero")

clustering

summary(clustering)

# Plot clustering coefficient distribution
hist(clustering,
     main = "Clustering coefficient distribution",
     xlab = "Clustering coefficient",
     ylab = "Number of nodes")
```

## Compare with a model network

We will generate a random network (Erdos-Renyi) and compare it to the microbiome network above.

```{r}
# Generate an Erdos-Renyi network with the same number of nodes and edges
# Erdos-Renyi model network
g_er <- sample_gnm(vcount(g), ecount(g), directed = TRUE)

# Compute degree for the model network
deg_er <- degree(g_er)

# Compare distributions
hist(deg, col = "cyan",
     main = "Degree Comparison",
     xlab = "Degree",
     ylab = "Number of nodes")

hist(deg_er, col = "purple", add = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Compute clustering coefficient for the model network
clustering_er <- transitivity(g_er,
                              type = "local",
                              isolates = "zero")

clustering_er

summary(clustering_er)

# Compare clustering coefficient distributions
hist(clustering,
     col = "cyan",
     main = "Clustering Coefficient Comparison",
     xlab = "Clustering coefficient",
     ylab = "Number of nodes")

hist(clustering_er,
     col = "purple",
     add = TRUE)
```
